saints.name: St. Edward the Confessor
saints.title: King
saints.shortBlurb: The pious last king of the House of Wessex, remembered for gentleness, generosity, and the building of Westminster Abbey…
biography: Born in 1003, a son of King Æthelred II and Emma of Normandy, Edward spent his youth in Norman exile while Danish kings ruled England, and was called to the throne in 1042. His twenty-four-year reign was one of almost unbroken peace: he remitted the Danegelt tax, gave largely to the poor, and was the first English king to touch for the king's evil.

Bound by a vow of chastity, he married Edith, Earl Godwin's daughter, only on her agreement to live with him as a sister, the memory of which, with the strains of that alliance, later made him a patron of difficult marriages. A vowed pilgrimage to Rome being commuted by the pope, he rebuilt instead the abbey of St. Peter at Westminster, dedicated but a week before his death.

He died on 5 January 1066, leaving the succession that ended in the Norman Conquest, and was buried in his abbey. Canonized by Alexander III in 1161, his body was found incorrupt and translated by Thomas Becket on 13 October 1163, the day of his feast. He remained a patron of England and of kings until St. George took his place in the fourteenth century.
saints.knownFor: Piety as king and the founding of Westminster Abbey.
